title: Explaining Problems

expressions.example: That's why I've been calling every day.
Because of that, we lost the client.
So, we decided to report the issue.
I've been having trouble with my internet.

sentences: I've been having trouble with my internet, so I called support.
The system crashed because it hasn't been updated.
We've been waiting for a week, that's why we're frustrated.
She's been working overtime because of the deadline.
Because the shipment was delayed, we lost the client.
I've been trying to fix this for hours, so I need help.
That's why I've been calling customer service every day.
The machine has been malfunctioning, so we reported it.

grammar.title: Cause & Effect — Because / So / That's Why + Present Perfect Continuous
rules: "Because" introduz a causa: The system crashed because it hasn't been updated.
"So" introduz a consequência: It broke, so we called support.
"That's why" resume a razão de forma mais natural na fala: That's why we're frustrated.
Present perfect continuous (have/has been + V-ing) mostra uma ação contínua até o momento presente, útil para explicar um problema em andamento.

rows: It crashed because it wasn't updated.
vem antes ou depois da consequência
It broke, so we called support.
I've been having trouble with it.
